questions.q: Who meets Jarvis and his wife at the airport in Johannesburg?
choices: John Harrison, the brother of Arthur's wife Mary
questions.explain: John says of Arthur, 'the finest man I ever knew.'

questions.q: Where are Mary and the grandchildren staying?
choices: At the Harrisons' — Mary's parents' home, where Jarvis and his wife will also stay
questions.explain: Looking after the badly-shaken children 'has given Mary something to occupy herself.'

questions.q: When is the funeral arranged for?
choices: The next afternoon at three o'clock, after a service in the Parkwold Church
questions.explain: Harrison and John have arranged it 'provisionally.'

questions.q: What kind of messages of sympathy have poured in for Arthur?
choices: From the Bishop, the Acting Prime Minister, the Mayor — and also from native organisations, coloured people, Indians and Jews
None; the death is being kept quiet
questions.explain: A 'sad pride' rises in Jarvis at the range of people his son had touched.

questions.q: What causes had Arthur Jarvis taken up publicly?
choices: Native crime, more Native schools, conditions at the non-European Hospital, and the mine compound system — he wanted settled labour with wife and family
questions.explain: There had even been talk of getting him to stand as a native M.P.

questions.q: What had Hathaway of the Chamber of Mines asked Harrison to do?
choices: Warn Arthur to 'pipe down a bit', because his firm did a lot of business with the Mines
questions.explain: Arthur's reply, through Mary: 'it's more important to speak the truth than to make money.'

questions.q: How does Jarvis privately regard the picture of his son that emerges from Harrison's talk?
choices: As exactly the son he knew
As 'a stranger' — 'this boy of his had gone journeying in strange waters, further than his parents had known'
questions.explain: He suspects his son's mother may have understood him better.

questions.q: What does Jarvis privately admit about his own view of missionaries and such work?
choices: He had 'never thought much of missionaries', and remembered the Ndotsheni mission only as a 'sad', dirty, forlorn place
He had funded it generously for years
questions.explain: Yet he finds himself calling his own son 'a missionary.'

questions.q: In bed that night, what does Margaret say about what she has heard of Arthur's work?
choices: 'It makes me proud' — and she reminds James she always knew he was like that
questions.explain: She had always been nearer to their son than James was.

questions.q: What does Jarvis whisper to his wife about his son's life and ideas?
choices: 'I'm sorry I didn't understand it... I didn't know it would ever be so important to understand it.'
questions.explain: There remains 'one thing I don't understand, why it should have happened to him.'
